A quick update: our design team is looking at a 'Large' display mode for tablets that would increase both checkbox and text size. I've added your ticket to that project so you'll hear when it's available to try.

Kind regards,
Bailey Adams

tickets.subject: How do reminders work across time zones?

messages.body:
Hi,

I'm a chef and travel between Lisbon and New York a lot for work. I set reminders for things like ordering produce, but I can't find any docs on whether a 7am reminder follows me to the new time zone or stays at 7am Lisbon time. A couple of my reminders went off at weird hours last trip. Is this explained anywhere?

Obrigado,
Roberto Gallo

Hi Roberto,

Great question, and you're right that our help center doesn't explain this well. By default, reminders follow your device's current time zone, so 7am stays 7am local wherever you are. If you want a reminder fixed to a specific zone, open the reminder, tap 'Time zone', and choose one. I've asked our docs team to add a proper article about this.

Best,
Drew Adams

Thanks,
Jacob Stein

Best,
Avery Adams

tickets.subject: Unchecked task doesn't go back to its original spot

messages.body:

On my iPad I keep our 'Closing Checklist' in a specific order. When a task is checked off it moves to the bottom, which is fine, but when I uncheck it, it stays at the bottom instead of going back where it was. My staff then work through the checklist out of order. Can unchecking put the task back in its original position?

Carlos Mendes

Thanks,
Ellis Adams

Thanks,
Ellis Adams

tickets.subject: Due dates shift back a day after refresh in Firefox

messages.body:
Hello,

I use the web app in Firefox to plan assignments for my classes. When I set a due date, say Friday the 10th, it looks right until I refresh the page, and then it shows Thursday the 9th. This happens on every task I've tried. My students see the wrong dates on our shared list too. I'm in the Central time zone, if that matters.

Marcus Odell

Hi Marcus,

Thanks for the details, and the time zone info helps. This looks like the date being saved as midnight UTC and then displayed in Central time, which pushes it back a day. I've escalated it to engineering. Could you check whether the same thing happens in Chrome? That will help us figure out whether it's specific to Firefox.

Best,
Casey Adams

Blessings,

Robert Nguyen

tickets.subject: Request: understand Spanish dates when typing tasks

messages.body: Hola! I teach English, Spanish and French and I write a lot of my tasks in Spanish. When I type "Calificar exámenes mañana" or "Reunión de padres el viernes", Q-DO doesn't pick up the date the way it does with "tomorrow" or "Friday" in English. I end up switching languages mid-thought just to get the due date set. Could you add natural-language date parsing for Spanish (and ideally French too)? It would save me a lot of clicks every day.

Hi Daniela, thanks for the detailed examples. Right now quick-add date detection only understands English phrases, so "mañana" and "el viernes" are treated as plain text. I've logged a feature request for Spanish and French date parsing and attached your examples so the team can test against them. In the meantime, the calendar picker next to the task field is the quickest way to set a date without switching languages. I'll update you if this gets scheduled.

tickets.subject: No docs on turning off notification emails for a single list

messages.body: Hi, I manage about a dozen shared lists for different projects, and a couple of them are very busy. I get an email every time someone checks something off, which is fine for my main project but overwhelming for the others. I searched the help center for how to mute notifications for just one list and only found the account-wide email toggle. Is per-list control possible? If so, can it be documented somewhere?

Hi Delphine, good catch, this isn't covered in the help center yet. You can mute email notifications for an individual list: open the list, tap the three-dot menu in the top right, choose List settings > Notifications, and switch "Email me about activity" off. Your account-wide settings stay as they are for every other list. I've asked our docs team to add a section on per-list notifications to the Sharing & Notifications article.

tickets.subject: Setup won't continue without contacts permission

messages.body: Hello, I just installed Q-DO on my iPhone and the setup gets stuck on a screen asking for access to my contacts. I work in insurance and my contacts are client information, so I don't want to share them with any app. If I tap Don't Allow, it just brings me back to the same screen and I can't get past it. Is there a way to finish setup without granting this?

Hi Desiree, I completely understand, and contacts access is not required to use Q-DO. It's only used to suggest people when sharing lists. On that screen there should be a small "Skip for now" link below the Continue button; in version 4.2.0 it can be hidden if your phone's text size is set to large. Please update to 4.2.1 from the App Store, which fixes that layout, and you'll be able to skip the step. You can always share lists by typing an email address instead.

tickets.subject: Q-DO not showing in Amazon Appstore on Kindle Fire

messages.body: Hi there, I wanted to put Q-DO on my Kindle Fire so the kids and I can share our chore lists, but when I search the Amazon Appstore it doesn't show up at all. Is there another way to install it on this tablet? I'm not very familiar with Kindle settings.

Hi Caroline, thanks for reaching out. Q-DO isn't currently published in the Amazon Appstore, so it won't appear in search. The easiest option on a Kindle Fire is our web app: open the Silk browser, go to app.q-do.com, sign in, and then tap the menu and choose "Add to Home" so it gets an icon like a regular app. Your shared chore lists will work the same as on the phone app.
Thank you! I added it to the home screen. One thing though, my 9-year-old doesn't have her own email. Can she still check things off on our shared list?

Great to hear it's working! Every person on a shared list needs their own Q-DO account, but since the Kindle is a family device, the simplest approach is for her to use it while signed in to your account. If you'd like her to have her own sign-in later, you can create an account for her using a parent-managed address and share the chore list with edit permission.
Perfect, that works for us for now. Thanks so much for the help!
You're very welcome, Caroline. I'll mark this as solved, but feel free to reply if anything else comes up. Happy chore-checking!

tickets.subject: Desktop app asking for a server URL on first launch

messages.body: I just installed the Q-DO desktop app on my Windows laptop (version 3.8.2) before heading out to a field site. On first launch it shows a "Server URL" field and won't let me continue without filling it in. I've only ever used Q-DO on my phone and have no idea what server I'm supposed to enter. What goes here?

Hi Ibrahim, sorry for the confusion. That field is meant for organizations running a self-hosted setup, and it should be hidden for regular accounts. Click the "Use Q-DO cloud" link just under the field (or enter https://app.q-do.com) and you'll go straight to the normal sign-in, where your phone account will work. We're fixing the first-run screen in the next release so this won't appear by default.

tickets.subject: Custom app icons for iOS?

messages.body: Hi Q-DO team! I'm a designer and I keep my iPhone home screen pretty curated, neutral tones, minimal icons. The bright Q-DO icon really stands out (in a bad way, sorry!). A lot of apps now offer alternate icons in settings. Any chance you could add a few options, like a monochrome or dark version? I'd even happily share some design ideas.

Hi Jessica, no apology needed, that's great feedback. Alternate app icons aren't available yet, but I've added your request to our tracker with a note about monochrome and dark variants. On iOS 18 and later you can also long-press the home screen, tap Edit > Customize, and choose Dark or Tinted, which our icon supports. We'll let you know if custom icons make it onto the roadmap.

tickets.subject: Task comment times showing in UTC instead of Accra time

messages.body: Good day. I use Q-DO with my church leadership team to coordinate our weekly programs, and we leave comments on tasks to discuss details. On my Android 13 phone, every comment timestamp is shown in UTC rather than my local time here in Accra. The due dates on tasks look correct, it is only the comments. Kindly assist.
Hello Emmanuel, thank you for reporting this. Could you tell me which version of Q-DO you have installed (Settings > About) and whether your phone's time zone is set automatically or manually?
Thank you for the quick reply. The app version is 5.1.4 and the time zone is set automatically. It shows GMT+00:00 Accra in my phone settings.

Thanks, that's very helpful. Since Accra is GMT+0 all year, the times should actually match UTC. Could you send an example of a comment where the time looks wrong, along with what time you expected to see?

I see. Yesterday I posted a comment at about 4:15 in the afternoon and it shows 16:15 UTC with the word UTC beside it, while my other team members in London see it as 17:15. The time itself is right, but it says UTC instead of my local time format.

Thank you, that clarifies it. The app is labelling comment times with "UTC" and using 24-hour format instead of your local time label and your phone's 12-hour setting. I've reproduced this on Android 13 and passed it to our mobile team as a display bug. I'll keep this ticket open and update you once a fix is released.
Much appreciated. God bless.
You're welcome, Emmanuel. We'll be in touch soon.
